notes: On 26 June 2025, and for three days, hundreds of residents barricaded streets with concrete or wooden blocks and burning tires and clashed with security forces (including police and military) in several neighborhoods of Lome (Lome, Lome Commune, Maritime) during demonstrations against the country's constitutional reform, the erosion of freedoms, the high cost of living, and the repression of dissenting voices. Some demonstrators threw projectiles at security forces. Police dispersed demonstrators using tear gas in several neighborhoods. In the Atiegou neighborhood, soldiers shot dead a man while residents reported to have been beaten, and tear gassed inside their homes. Armed men (described as paid militiamen) partially wearing baklavas and in unregistered vehicles were said to have operated alongside security forces. The authorities deployed a large security presence, with patrols visible on all major roads. Several social media platforms were also temporarily blocked, including Facebook and Telegram. The demonstrations, lasting from 26 June - 28 June, resulted in hundreds of people injured, several of them seriously. Between 60 and 100 people were arrested, including arbitrary arrests, some of whom were released, and some disappeared. Journalists were also arrested and their images deleted.7 bodies were found dead in the lagoons and a lake in Lome (4 were recovered on 27 June and 3 on 28 June), suspected to have been killed by security forces. The government denied this. 1 fatality coded to this event.
